note: Corpus Corporum's transcription only — Migne's plate is not touched. Verified against the plate: archive.org patrologiaecurs04migngoog (on disk raw/scans/pl113/), PDF page = (column + 11) / 2, calibrated this session against the printed corner numbers (p. 287 = cols 563/564). Read at 450 dpi on crops taken wider than the target word, whole line read at each.
class: Three digitization corruptions, all NON-WORDS in our file and all confirmed as ours — two letter transpositions (Paralimopenis/Paralipomenis, raeedificabant/reaedificabant, the latter standing where Migne hyphenates reaedifi-/cabant) and one substitution (cupuditati/cupiditati). None had been marked [sic:]; the translator raised all four of this work's non-words as plate candidates and fired nothing, per the ship test.

patches.why: the plate prints 'Legitur enim in Paralipomenis quod Athalia et filii ejus' — the book of Chronicles, which is what the sentence cites. 'Paralimopenis' is no word in any language; m/p transposition.

the plate prints 'quae per haeresim et schismata rupta erant reædifi-' at the line end, 'cabant' at the head of the next. Our file transposed the vowels of the prefix. ⚑ The hyphenated break is Migne's own and is not represented in our reflowed text, so only the letters are corrected.
the plate prints 'quos populus terrae, scilicet terrenae cupiditati dediti' — earthly DESIRE, which the whole gloss is about. 'cupuditati' is no Latin word.

scan_note: ⚠ THIS COPY OF PL 113 CLIPS THE LEFT MARGIN ON SOME PAGES — confirmed on p. 320 and p. 354, where the left column's opening characters are cut. It does NOT affect the right column, and most pages are clean. Practical consequence: a non-word standing at the START of a left-column line may be unreadable here while its neighbours read perfectly, and that is a property of our copy, not of Migne's plate. Check the left edge before recording an illegible.

resolved_by_second_witness.verdict: MIGNE'S OWN PLATE — NO PATCH. Settled 2026-08-24 against a SECOND WITNESS after our archive.org copy proved clipped: Gallica bpt6k5505319w, f = (column + 1) / 2, calibrated against the printed corner numbers before the read. The Gallica scan carries the full left margin and prints '- ulit Saraiam, qui interpretatur vinctus, sacer-' with only a broken fragment of a raised stroke where the T should be. ⭐ The contrast is on the same page: 'VERS. 18. -- Tulit quoque.' prints its T cleanly two lines above. So the lost initial is a FAILED SORT IN MIGNE'S FORME, not a loss of Corpus Corporum's -- our source transcribed him faithfully, and there is nothing to patch.
resolved_by_second_witness.consequence: The English marker was CHANGED from [cj:] to [sic: ulit]. With the plate in hand the defect is demonstrably the plate's own, which is exactly what [sic:] exists to record and exactly what it must not claim without evidence. The marker-strip test passes: delete it and 'He took Saraias' still has its verb and its object.
